stories.primary_headline: Power supply hit in Gurugram, Faridabad and Nuh as workers strike over privatisation

primary_source.headline: Power supply hit in Gurugram, Faridabad and Nuh as workers strike over privatisation
primary_source.content: Gurugram: A strike by Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam (DHBVN) workers plunged Gurugram, Faridabad, and Nuh districts into darkness since 10 pm on Wednesday, affecting thousands of consumers and industrial units.The power department received more than 3,000 complaints of outages within 12 hours of the strike, an official said on condition of anonymity on Thursday.The employees had announced the strike to protest against the Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission's decision to grant a parallel electricity distribution licence to a private company for Gurugram and Nuh districts.Gurugram Deputy Commissioner Uttam Singh held a meeting with the employees till late at night, urging them to reconsider their decision. However, the talks proved inconclusive, and no agreement was reached to end the strike.Several industrial units in Gurugram came to a standstill due to prolonged power cuts, with many owners complaining of potential losses running to crores of rupees.Deepak Maini, an industrialist and the chairman of the Progressive Federation of Trade and Industry, said there had been no power supply at Gurugram’s Sector-37 since 10 pm on Wednesday.Maini also expressed concern that any delay in the restoration of power supply could adversely affect production and business activities.He said that the availability of finished goods and the timely delivery of supplies could also be affected.“Power cuts at industrial units have brought machinery and production to a halt, impacting business operations. With operations suspended across hundreds of units, the risk of losses has increased,” Maini said.Apart from Gurugram, industrial units in Kadipur and Basai were also affected by power cuts.Ahmedabad Crime Branch catches MP man wanted in murder of six persons from GurugramSeveral residential colonies in Gurugram had to switch to generators as inverter backups ran out, residents said.In many areas, the breakdown of the power supply led to a shortage of drinking water. Residents say they are managing using water stored in tanks but claim that it will last only a few hours."Electricity and water are both essential services. Where is the government? Residents are held hostage by DHBVN staff. There has been no power since 10 pm yesterday. Either the government should settle employees' demands or depute the Disaster Management team to restore the supply. Officers are also showing helplessness. In such a situation, how will we come up with a solution?” said Shiv Kumar Sharma, a resident.In Faridabad, people in the New Industrial Township-2 area hit the streets, demanding restoration of power supply. They said the power cut also impacted water supply.Upon hearing information of a road blockade, police arrived at the scene and pacified the protesters, following which they were dispersed.In Nuh district, the power outage severely affected life in several areas, including Punhana, Nagina, and Firozpur Jhirka.Despite several attempts, the Superintending Engineer of the Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam (DHBVN), Operation Circle Gurugram-I, could not be contacted.

'Pak Didn't Accept Bodies Of Its Own Soldiers In Kargil': India Slams UN Rapporteur

brief_bullets: At a United Nations interactive dialogue, India’s First Secretary Bhavika Mangalanandan sharply rebuked Pakistan for its hypocrisy regarding religious freedom and funeral rights. Responding to a UN report criticizing India’s security operations in Jammu and Kashmir, Mangalanandan highlighted that Pakistan famously refused to claim its own soldiers killed during the 1999 Kargil War, forcing the Indian Army to provide them with dignified Islamic burials. She further dismissed the UN rapporteur’s findings as unsupported, arguing that Pakistan lacks the moral standing to lecture India on human rights while its own minorities face systemic abuse. India maintains that sovereign states must retain the legal authority to restrict funeral rites for terrorists who violate the fundamental right to life.
why_it_matters_bullets: This diplomatic confrontation underscores India's aggressive strategy to delegitimize Pakistan's international advocacy by exposing its historical and domestic contradictions.

stories.primary_headline: Watch: Met chief Rowley not fit for job, says detective raped by colleague

primary_source.headline: Watch: Met chief Rowley not fit for job, says detective raped by colleague
primary_source.content: A Met Police detective who was raped by a fellow officer has said the force's handling of her case was "like being raped all over again". Det Con Linda Williams was attacked in 2004 by PC David Carrick - who was jailed for life in 2023 for sexual offences against her and 11 others. Linda sought damages from the Met for failing to protect her from Carrick and said the process left her feeling suicidal. She now wants Met Commissioner, Sir Mark Rowley, to resign because he has failed to change police culture as promised. Investigations correspondent Daniel De Simone reports.
